beats.text: December 1900. Three lighthouse keepers on a tiny island, twenty miles off the coast of Scotland. Then the light went dark.
When the relief boat finally arrived, nobody came down to meet it.
Inside, the clock had stopped. The lamp had been cleaned and filled, ready for dusk. Nobody lit it.
In the lobby, two sets of oilskin coats were missing. The third was still on its hook.
At the west landing, a storm had smashed a box of ropes a hundred and ten feet above the sea.
The investigator concluded the last man had left in a hurry, without his coat. Perhaps to warn the other two.
None of the three was ever found. What would make a careful keeper run out without his coat?
